item.title: A C.J. Stroud flu game? Sick and with the chills, Texans QB throws for 5 TDs to beat Chargers
item.description: Back in his native Southern California, C.J. Stroud turned in one of the best games of his career as the Texans stayed in the playoff hunt with a win over the Chargers. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) INGLEWOOD, Calif. - When C.J. Stroud woke up in his hotel bed Sunday morning in downtown Los Angeles, he was still feeling under the weather. All week he had been dealing with some kind of illness that he said gave him chills and "all the things." He said he barely practiced Thursday. Whatever he had, it was still with him. Yet, some six hours later, he went on to have one of the best games of his career. Stroud, who was playing in front of friends and family near his hometown of Rancho Cucamonga , threw for a season-high 384 yards, a career-high five touchdowns and just one interception in Houston's 44-22 rout of the Los Angeles Chargers (0-8) on Sunday afternoon at SoFi Stadium. Texans Insider with Jonathan M. Alexander Sign up for an in-depth newsletter with Houston Texans news, features and predictions. The 44 points scored were a season high for the Texans' offense, which has often delivered time and time again, especially on the road. The Texans improved to 3-5 on the season. It was the type of performance that will put Stroud in the MVP conversation if he can continue playing this way. It is the type of performance that will have some suggesting that the Texans can make a run towards the playoffs. "He really gives that confidence to the entire team," coach DeMeco Ryans said of Stroud. "When the defensive guys, they see him up making plays, everyone is excited. Everyone knows the type of energy, the type of momentum that that brings to our entire team when he's making those plays and he's done it all year." The Texans are currently 1 ½ games behind the Patriots for that final wild-card spot with nine games remaining. They face the Browns, who are also 1 ½ games ahead of them, next Sunday in Cleveland. But based on their upcoming schedule, and how Stroud is playing, anything is possible, especially if the defense can gain some momentum too. Though the performance from the defense wasn't perfect, Sunday's game against the NFL's worst offense was a step in the right direction. The Texans tied a franchise record with eight sacks on Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert. They also forced two turnovers - an interception by cornerback Derek Stingley Jr. and a fumble. But the offense, which had 485 yards of total offense, was the story of this game. And it started with Stroud, who became just the fourth quarterback younger than 26 years old with at least 350 passing yards and five touchdown passes in multiple games, joining Patrick Mahomes, Dan Marino and Matthew Stafford. The other game Stroud achieved that stat line was during his 2023 rookie season, when he threw five touchdowns in a thrilling 39-37 win over the Bucs . item.description: Texas Longhorns defensive back Graceson Littleton (29) and Texas Longhorns linebacker Justin Cryer (28) defend Missouri Tigers wide receiver Cayden Lee (19) during the game against Missouri at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium in Columbia on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. (Mikala Compton/Austin American-Statesman) COLUMBIA, Mo. - The chatter started before Texas football even joined the SEC. The conference is too rugged, the league's old guard said. The road trips are too grueling. And the Longhorns, with their abundance of resources and Big 12 background, are just too soft. But as the team proved yet again in Saturday's 34-20 win at No. 18 Missouri, No. 7 Texas (7-2, 4-2 SEC) has the steel needed for a run at the College Football Playoff. The Longhorns improved to 7-2 in true SEC road games since joining the conference in 2024, a rate of success that must impress even the most ardent burnt-orange skeptic. "Our guys, they're not naive to noise," Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said after Saturday's win. "As much as I would love to say, ‘Hey, tune it all out,' I could hear the talk getting on the plane (Friday). I could hear the talk when we got here. Nobody thought we were going to come here and win the game. Nobody thought we were tough enough at the line of scrimmage. Everyone thought we'd get pushed around." But in a slugfest that felt much closer than the final score, Texas ran for 107 yards on 23 carries before taking away sacks yardage and held the SEC's leading rusher in Jamal Roberts to 66 yards on 19 carries. In the process, the Longhorns silenced a sold-out crowd at Memorial Stadium that craved a win over its former Big 12 tormentor. item.title: ‘We call him…’: Bones Hyland says T-Wolves have a new nickname for Joan Beringer after his 'broken nose'
item.description: Photo by David Berding/Getty Images The Minnesota Timberwolves made it four wins in a row after beating the Utah Jazz 115-100. LaMelo Ball stole the show as he always does, while Ayo Dosunmu scored 26 points. But the bench more than played its part, especially Bones Hyland and Joan Beringer. The former has a nickname for the Frenchman now. Bones Hyland says Joan Beringer is called ‘The Batman’ and shares a ‘funny story’ Beringer suffered a nasal fracture during the Minnesota Timberwolves’ win over the New Orleans Pelicans in the NBA Cup. The Frenchman suffered an inadvertent elbow to his face. He still scored two free throws with blood coming out of his nose, but he didn’t return after being diagnosed with a fracture. There were fears that Beringer would be sidelined, but the teenager played against the Jazz on Sunday night while wearing a protective mask. Hyland claimed that Beringer even wore the mask in the locker room when he first got it, thus leading to a new nickname. He said: “We call him ‘The Batman’. It’s a funny story. We were in the locker room, and he had that mask on. They told him he had to wear it. He ain’t take it off in the locker room. “I was like: ‘Joan, you ain’t even on the court right now. You can take your mask off’. But that was the first time he was wearing the mask with a broken nose. “But he’s a warrior, bro. We love Joan. He has come in with young legs and runs the floor for us, blocks shots, and makes shots go left or right. We love Joan!” ‘The Batman’ is a really cool nickname for Beringer, but what’s better is his performances for the Minnesota Timberwolves this season. The teenager has impressed everyone and has earned a lot of praise, including one from his country’s biggest basketball star, Victor Wembanyama. Beringer is not a starter yet, but if he keeps developing at the same rate, he will become a star in the not-too-distant future. item.title: Nick Wright calls Patrick Mahomes a ‘cyborg’ after getting injured with hit during Chiefs win over Jets
item.description: Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes pushed through a serious hit in their 35-12 win over the New York Jets. Mahomes did not miss a single offensive snap in the win, going 23/31 on pass attempts for 242 yards, two TDs, and a 117.9 passer rating. He also rushed for eight yards on two carries in a strong performance. Mahomes was tackled by Jets EDGE David Bailey in the second quarter and appeared to suffer an elbow injury, but his resolute toughness made him push through the discomfort and finish the win after avoiding major injury. Patrick Mahomes hailed as a cyborg by Nick Wright Watching Mahomes take that rough hit and escape without injury left FOX Sports’ Nick Wright in awe of the 33-year-old QB. “Also… Never a doubt. Mahomes is a cyborg. 99% of QBs have their elbow dislocated on that hit. He missed zero snaps. They’ll be 8-2 heading into Buffalo.” It’s since been confirmed that Mahomes’ injury is an elbow strain/sprain after post-game MRIs, with the QB likely not missing their game against the Atlanta Falcons on November 15. Mahomes admitted after the win that the hit from Bailey had a major impact on his performance, as he struggled to throw the ball as deep and precisely as he normally can. Nonetheless, even a slightly wounded Mahomes would be a better option than backup QB Justin Fields for the Chiefs right now, especially as they look to challenge the 7-2 Denver Broncos for THE top spot in the AFC West. While Mahomes has not been among the MVP contenders this season, he has had a strong comeback season after rushing through recovery from a torn ACL. Over the season, Mahomes has thrown 177/263 for 2,037 yards, 14 TDs, and four INTs for a 101.8 passer rating. Avoiding a season-ending elbow injury on that play was a moment of good fortune for the Chiefs, and the franchise will hope that fortune pushes them through till the end of the season. item.title: Three-time Olympic judo champion announces bid for French presidency
item.description: Three-time Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner is to run for the French presidency, with his campaign intending to “show that we can turn France around”. The 37-year-old said he would not run on a left- or right-wing ticket but instead focus his campaign on “bringing the French people together”, with the slogan for his campaign “The France we want”. He told French outlet Le Parisien on Monday: “France is a great country. It has allowed me to become the person I am today and has given me the opportunity to dream big. “Today, that’s what’s missing. That ambition is gone; that hope is gone. “I see a divide in society across the country, but I do not accept what I hear in the mouths of young people, that it is difficult today to imagine a future. That is why I decided to commit myself, alongside the French people, and to become a candidate for the presidency.” Riner has no experience of politics but is a well-known and popular figure in France, and has previously hinted at a desire to enter politics at the highest level. He said in an interview last year: “I am a citizen above all, not just a sportsperson. If tomorrow I enter politics, it wouldn’t be to be a minister, it would be to change things. The best role would be president.” Riner, who was born in Guadeloupe, grew up in Paris. He is a nine-time heavyweight world champion, two-time openweight world champion, and has two Olympic bronze medals to go with his three individual golds and two mixed team gold medals. He was a torchbearer during the Olympic torch relay ahead of the 2024 Games in Paris, and lit the cauldron during the opening ceremony alongside retired sprinter Marie-Jose Perec. Riner said that the experience of the home Olympic Games uniting the country inspired him to enter politics, saying: “I saw a whole country come together, proud, happy. I thought to myself, what we have been able to do for 15 days, we must be able to do for the country.” He said his decision to run for president would not end his judo career or hopes of competing at the LA Games 2028.

Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs picked up a dominant 35-12 win over the New York Jets on Sunday, but they had a scary moment along the way as superstar quarterback Patrick Mahomes took a big hit to his throwing arm in the second quarter. For a moment, it looked like he could be seriously hurt. Mahomes was able to stay in the game, and an MRI reportedly didn’t reveal any major injury. But after the game, the Chiefs star admitted that the moment scared him, especially after the knee injury that ended his season last year. Mahomes’ Injury Scare Late in the second quarter, Jets edge rusher David Bailey hit Mahomes’ right arm as he was throwing, with Will McDonald IV and Darrell Jackson Jr. also getting a piece of him on the play. Mahomes grimaced on the ground and then walked off slowly with his arm hanging at his side. But Mahomes flexed his elbow on the sideline, threw a few warm-up passes, and returned without missing a snap. Chiefs assistant athletic trainer Julie Frymyer worked on his arm at halftime, and head coach Andy Reid adjusted the game plan in the second half to lean on short throws. Mahomes finished 23 of 31 for 242 yards and two touchdowns, both of which came before the hit. After the game, sources told ESPN’s Ian Rapoport that an MRI didn’t show any major injury to Mahomes’ right elbow. The Chiefs will monitor it for pain and swelling ahead of next Sunday’s game against the Atlanta Falcons. ‘That stuff scares you’ Mahomes said after the game that he was always going to try to get back out there despite the injury. “If I’m able to play, I’m going to play,” Mahomes said, via ESPN’s Nate Taylor . “That’s part of the game. It scares you in moments, when you get some pains in certain areas of your body. Obviously, it didn’t feel great, but I was able to kind of get it worked on a little bit, especially at halftime.” He also admitted that the injury brought back memories of last season, when he tore his ACL and LCL in his left knee in December. “Any time it’s elbows and knees, it’s always scary, just because you just don’t know,” Mahomes said. “Even my knee last year, after we were doing the initial test, I thought, because I could walk off the field, I was going to be good. It is the kind of development that feels entirely in keeping with the times at Old Trafford. United’s league form has left them in an alarming position and, even with some encouragement on the European front, the domestic picture has looked fragile. item.description: Porto and Villa star identified as potential Liverpool star replacements Alisson Becker exit talk leaves Liverpool facing major goalkeeper succession questions Liverpool have a big call to make on Alisson Becker, and there is no point dressing it up. The report centres on Fabrizio Romano’s update that Alisson leaving when his contract expires next summer is now a genuine possibility. The key point here is simple, Liverpool are not in active renewal talks. For a player of Alisson’s level, that matters. Clubs do not drift into these situations by accident. item.description: Coco Gauff celebrates after defeating Jessica Pegula at Cincinnati Open at Lindner Family Tennis Center. © IMAGN via Reuters Connect Coco Gauff left Sunday’s 2026 WTA Finals court on good terms with Jessica Pegula. The two battled for three sets in the Group 1 match at Indian Wells before Gauff won. However, the match was clouded by controversy surrounding Pegula’s previous comparison between Gauff and Mirra Andreeva, leading into this encounter. During a practice-session livestream on the WTA’s YouTube channel, Pegula’s comments were unknowingly broadcast , where she compared Andreeva and Gauff. Pegula suggested that Andreeva is a better player and could surpass the two-time Grand Slam champion if she carried the same mentality. After Sunday’s showdown, Gauff was asked about Pegula’s comments. “Jess, she told me, before I even saw the video, she came and apologized immediately,” Gauff told reporters. “Honestly, I didn’t really take it. I feel like maybe the other person in the situation got a lot more of it. But she, you know, they both, even her coach, apologized to me. So yeah, I think for me, I’m a competitor, so I’m always going to compete regardless of what’s happening off the court. But yeah, I know her heart, and it was all good. I don’t feel any type of way.” Earlier on Friday, two days after her private conversation was leaked, Pegula shared that it was unfortunate and admitted she had contacted both individuals about it. Meanwhile, the WTA also apologized for failing to inform players that microphones were active. Furthermore, Pegula, who had criticized Andreeva’s attitude and relationship with coach Conchita Martínez, exchanged humorous Instagram comments with the Russian teenager. Jessica Pegula Explains Reason Behind WTA Finals Loss to Coco Gauff Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula’s WTA Finals Group 1 match lasted for two hours and 39 minutes. In the end, Gauff, who saved multiple break points in the opening set and came back from a 5-2 deficit in the second set, won 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-2. In the third set, it was evident that Pegula was exhausted as Gauff raced to a 3-0 lead. The two-time Grand Slam champion ended up winning the set and is now 1-0 in Group 1 matches. item.description: Journalist suggests despite assist Liverpool star upsets balance of team Lynch suggests Liverpool star upsets team balance despite assist Dominik Szoboszlai’s assist against Crystal Palace did not resolve the questions surrounding his place in Liverpool’s midfield, according to David Lynch. Speaking on Anfield Index’s Media Matters podcast, the journalist argued that the Hungarian’s contribution from deliveries into the penalty area should not obscure concerns about his positioning, pressing and passing in deeper areas. Liverpool secured another away victory, but Lynch felt their midfield remained too easy to play through. For him, the result and individual attacking returns should be assessed alongside the quality of the overall performance. Szoboszlai’s contribution leaves wider questions Lynch’s criticism centred on whether Szoboszlai currently gives Liverpool enough across every phase of the game. “I think you can’t carry a player purely for set-piece threat. You just can’t,” he said. Discussing the midfielder’s chances created, Lynch suggested most, if not all, had originated from set-piece situations. His broader concern was what happened between those deliveries, when Liverpool needed to retain possession, advance through midfield and prevent Palace from breaking forward. “You can’t put someone in the XI just for the set-piece threat because the fact is you’ve got to carry them then through the phases of the game,” he added. That does not diminish the value of an assist. It questions whether the attacking reward compensates for difficulties elsewhere in the team. Pressing and passing require improvement Lynch highlighted two areas raised by Daniel Sturridge before the match: pressing more intelligently and showing greater ambition when passing through opposition lines. “He wanted him to press smarter and he wanted him to take more risks with the ball in terms of firing it through the lines, breaking lines, getting it into the final third,” Lynch said. “He has that passing range, but he’s way too safe in it sometimes, and so he doesn’t progress the ball quickly enough.” For Lynch, energetic running does not always translate into effective defending. Arriving too quickly can allow an opponent to escape pressure, leaving the midfielder unable to make a meaningful challenge. item.title: Berkhamsted players banned from watching FA Cup draw
item.description: The manager of seventh-tier Berkhamsted says his players have been banned from the "distraction" of the FA Cup second round draw. The Hertfordshire club travel to fellow Southern League Premier Division South side Plymouth Parkway in the final tie of the first round on Monday, with the draw to be made ahead of the 19:30 kick-off. The tie will be broadcast to an international television audience, and, like their hosts, Berkhamsted have never previously reached this stage of the competition. "I've told the players they're not allowed anywhere near it [the draw]. Someone could tell me if they want who we get. I'm not really bothered about it," said Comrades boss Chris Devane. Plymouth Parkway players dream of glamorous FA Cup tie "It's important the players are focused on what they're there to do and that's win a football game. There's no point losing focus about who you may play if you do win, if you end up jeopardising the opportunity to win by doing so. "The players will be nowhere near it. I've told them all, let me deal with all the press, let me deal with the TV interviews. You guys have got a job to do. Let me worry about sweeping the floor, so to speak, so that's what the plan is." Berkhamsted, formed in 2009 after Berkhamsted Town folded, have beaten Bishop's Stortford, Hendon, Redditch United and Southend United to reach this stage - winning £20,625 from the FA's prize fund in the process. The winners of Monday's tie will take £47,750, with £15,800 going to the losers. Both clubs will also pocket £50,000 for the tie being selected for broadcast. The Comrades travelled down to Devon on Sunday, with their part-time players due to return home on Tuesday - and many needing to take unpaid leave from work. Speaking to BBC Three Counties Radio, Devane said: "I'm really intrigued to see how much will a proper day of rest, prep and pre-match meal actually helps them [my players]." item.title: ‘All-time embarrassment’ – Fans react as CBS Sports plays ‘Outstanding’ over New York Jets montage
item.description: Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Jets suffered yet another humiliating defeat, this time at the hands of the Kansas City Chiefs, but it was CBS that got to throw the most dirt on their name. As many expected, the Jets were comprehensively beaten by the Chiefs, with the final scoreline reading 35-12. This loss is the latest in a long string of defeats the Jets have suffered during HC Aaron Glenn’s second season, but one that still stings for the fanbase. Fans can’t believe CBS Sports used ‘washed-up’ anthem during New York Jets loss During their broadcast of the New York Jets vs. Kansas City Chiefs game, CBS Sports cut to commercial with a slow-motion montage of HC Aaron Glenn and QB Geno Smith showing their frustration. In an added layer of mockery, CBS Sports added Charlie Wilson’s song ‘Outstanding’ in the background – a song that has taken on a whole new meaning in the sports world over the last few years. While Wilson’s song is iconic, in recent years, it has become the unofficial anthem for players and teams who are far beyond their best years, and are no longer at the level they once were. Understandably, many fans took notice of what the broadcast team at CBS was doing, as they pointed out how humiliating it was for the Jets. One fan enlightened others about the significance of the song choice: “It means you’re washed up. When Kevin Garnett and Paul Pierce joined the Brooklyn Nets during the downside of their careers, they had a meme with this song playing.” Another fan added: “Bro had that s*** cued up and ready!” A third fan suggested Aaron Glenn was to blame: “This is an all-time embarrassment for the Jets. He might be worse than Adam Gase, and I didn’t think that was possible.” A fourth fan pointed to Glenn’s constant criticism of the referees: “The NFL saw the video of him holding the challenge flag all month long and decided to hand us another gem.” However, a fifth fan seemingly showed the Jets some sympathy: “Go ahead and pick on the little guy while he is down.” And lastly, one final fan had high praise for the CBS producers: “This may be the highest possible peak of NFL sports slander.” The Jets now find themselves 2-7 for the season, with no prospect of improvement on the horizon. For Jets fans, this marks yet another poor season. But there might be something to be hopeful about. As things stand, the Jets could have three possible first-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft, which could allow them to bring in some much-needed talent for the offensive unit and help them find a sense of direction going forward. item.title: Florida Panthers Struggling Against the Better Teams in the NHL
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Florida Panthers are off today before taking on the Columbus Blue Jackets on Tuesday night and, if recent trends hold up, the team’s two-game slide may come to an end in central Ohio. The Panthers have nine wins in their first 18 games. One of them was a 7-3 thrashing of the Blue Jackets a few weeks ago. The Blue Jackets are a team searching for an identity right now having lost three of five. They sit just below the .500 mark at 7-8-0. These are the kind of teams the Panthers have done well against this season. The better ones? Not so much. Of Florida’s nine wins this season, only two have come against teams currently holding a playoff position: The opener in OT against Carolina, and on Oct. 17 against Seattle. When you look at the current NHL playoff standings, you do not see a lot of teams that Florida has played. It is still very early in the season, after all. In fact, of the 15 teams holding a playoff spot (not counting the Panthers, who currently hold the final wild-card spot in the East), Florida has only played five of them. But of the ones they have played, the Panthers have not fared well. This weekend was another example. Although Washington is not a playoff team right now, the Capitals are finding their way and sit three points back of the Rangers for third in the Metro and are two back of the Panthers in the wild-card race. Florida lost 4-3 to the Capitals on Saturday. On Sunday, the Panthers took on the Atlantic-leading Bruins in Boston and fell behind 3-0 in the first before falling 4-1 . The Panthers do seem to be feasting on the Chicagos and Winnipegs of the world, with almost half of their nine wins coming in their four games with the Blackhawks and Jets. Throw in the Blue Jackets, Kings, and Canucks and it does feel like the Panthers are feasting on the lower end of the NHL while struggling when the competition ratchets up a bit. Again, it is very early in the season and the Panthers are right in the playoff mix. At 9-7-2, they are four points back of the Lightning for third in the division although Tampa Bay has played two fewer games. The Detroit Lions (6-2) are headed to Munich, Germany, to take on the New England Patriots (5-4) in an overseas edition of Week 10 NFL Football. It’s been 11 seasons since the Lions last played an international game, but this trip has been in the works for some time. In 2024, as part of the NFL’s Global Markets Program, the Lions have had marketing rights in the DACH region , which includes Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Since then, the team has made several trips to Germany and has helped support Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown— whose mother, Miriam Brown, was born and raised in Germany —in running youth football programs across the country. As for the game itself, it looks like it’ll be a good one, and the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -2.5 points . While the Lions are riding a four-game winning streak, the Patriots’ 2026 season has been a more up-and-down affair after reaching the Super Bowl in 2025. They opened the season by losing to the Seahawks, beat the Steelers, then lost to the Jaguars over the first three weeks. They got back to 2-2 with a big win over the Bills, then rallied to 4-2 after wins over the Raiders and Jets. The Bears took them down on Thursday night in Week 7, but the Patriots eeked out a five-point win over the Dolphins to reach 5-3. On Sunday, the Patriots took on the Packers and looked completely unprepared. Packer QB Jordan Love jumped all over them, throwing for 372 yards and three scores, while Patriots Drake Maye threw for 299 yards and three scores, but also threw three interceptions and was sacked four times. On the ground, the Packers’ worst-ranked rushing offense ran for 129 yards and two touchdowns, while the Pats gained 94 rushing yards, a touchdown, and lost a fumble. In the end, the Packers left Foxborough with a 45-27 win, and left former Patriots QB and current color commentator Tom Brady wondering who this New England team actually is: “Half the season they played like this, and the other half of the season they haven’t turned the ball over, they haven’t exposed the defense, have played more physical on defense, but right now it’s just too inconsistent. Which team are they going to get? The team that is loose with the ball, is loose with decision-making, looking like they can be beaten by anybody. Or the team that takes care of the football, that makes the other team play left-handed, and can do what they want to do. Can they be a good team? They haven’t quite done that because good teams leave the smallest margin of error.” The Lions and Patriots are scheduled to play on Sunday, November 15, at 9:30 a.m. ET at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany.

item.title: Ireland's Jansen ruled out of Fiji and Bok games
item.description: Jansen's home debut ended after just 46 minutes because of a knee injury [Getty Images] Sean Jansen has been ruled out of the remainder of Ireland's Nations Championship campaign with a knee injury, further depleting head coach Andy Farrell's options at number eight. With Caelan Doris and Jack Conan already injured, Jansen was forced off during Friday's 42-12 win over Argentina in Dublin and will return to Connacht to continue his rehabilitation. Centre Bundee Aki, a late withdrawal from the Argentina game with illness, is expected to resume full training on Tuesday. Farrell said Mack Hansen picked up an ankle problem in the Argentina game but the winger was not mentioned in the Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU)'s squad update on Monday. After facing Fiji and back-to-back world champions South Africa at Aviva Stadium, Ireland will travel to Twickenham for a finals weekend fixture. item.title: Late winner for Union St Gilloise from former Accrington Stanley defender puts more pressure on Genk head coach
item.description: Late winner for Union St Gilloise from former Accrington Stanley defender puts more pressure on Genk head coach Ross Sykes, a fan favourite for Union St Gilloise, made his first start since returning from time on the sidelines. item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Nic Claxton #9 of the Chicago Bulls poses for a photo during Chicago Bulls Media Day at the United Center on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty The wait is over. Nic Claxton made his Chicago debut on Sunday, and the Bulls center debut was a mix of promise and rust. The 6-foot-11 big man played just over 17 minutes off the bench in a 127-121 loss to the 76ers, finishing with four points, four rebounds, four assists and two blocks. The Bulls had waited more than a month for this look. Bulls Center Debut: Nic Claxton Shows Rim Protection Off the Bench Claxton missed the preseason and the first eight games with a left hamstring strain, so the plan was cautious. Coach Tiago Splitter kept him on the bench with a limit of about 16 to 20 minutes. He checked in late in the first quarter during a 10-2 Philadelphia run. Chicago acquired him in June in a three-way trade with Brooklyn and Minnesota. He’s 27, a seven-year veteran who averaged 11.7 points and 6.9 rebounds for the Nets last season. The defensive fit showed up quickly. Splitter often paired him with Noa Essengue, who picked up ball-handlers full-court while Claxton protected the rim behind him . That gave Chicago more pressure at the point of attack than it has had much of the season. His four assists were a good sign too. Rebounding Is Where the Rust Showed The glass was a different story. Philadelphia grabbed 20 offensive rebounds, eight of them by Joel Embiid, and Claxton gave up space to Embiid and Jabari Walker. He finished with four rebounds. He didn’t hide from it. Claxton said he “just gotta grab the ball” and keep an eye on who’s crashing. He also admitted the minutes limit helped. “I needed the restriction today,” he said with a laugh. Splitter called him gassed, which he said is normal for a first real game after a month. Why One Look Isn’t the Full Picture The restriction was respected, and it also meant Chicago got only a partial view. On a day when Splitter reshuffled his reserves, Claxton was the one new piece he got to add. The Bulls are 1-8 and have struggled defensively all season, so any help on that end matters. The instincts and timing were there. The stamina and rebounding will need more time and more minutes. As a Bulls center debut goes, useful but unfinished sums it up. That's crazy. Never let bitterness or pettiness get in front of your goals and dreams," Antetokounmpo said after the Heat's big Sunday win . item.description: Sep 14, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs place kicker Harrison Butker (7) prepares to kick the point after touchdown against the Denver Broncos during the game at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs rolled to a 35-12 win over the New York Jets on Sunday, but kicker Harrison Butker’s struggles continued as the once-automatic kicker missed yet another field goal and was booed by the home crowd at Arrowhead Stadium for the first time in his career. After the game, head coach Andy Reid wouldn’t commit to Butker as the team’s kicker going forward. And with Justin Tucker waiting on the practice squad, the longtime Chiefs kicker’s job could be in serious jeopardy. Butker’s Struggles Butker has been one of the most reliable kickers in the NFL for most of his career, and he made plenty of big kicks during the Chiefs’ three Super Bowl runs. But his accuracy has fallen off a cliff over the last two seasons. Just before halftime on Sunday, Butker sent a 51-yard attempt wide right. He now has seven missed field goals this season, the most in the NFL, and he has missed 17 kicks, including 12 field goals and five extra points, since the start of last season. The Chiefs held a kicker competition and then signed Tucker, a five-time All-Pro, to their practice squad two weeks ago. Tucker served a 10-game suspension last season for violating the league’s personal conduct policy after being accused of sexual misconduct by 16 massage therapists, and the signing sparked plenty of outrage . At the time, special teams coordinator Dave Toub insisted that Butker was still the kicker . “We’re trying to improve and get Butker right,” Toub said. “That’s what this whole thing is about.” Since then, though, Butker has continued to struggle, and he missed again on Sunday. ‘I’ve got to be better’ After Sunday’s game, Reid was asked about Butker’s future, and he certainly didn’t rule out the possibility of a change. “I’ll address that as we go throughout the week,” Reid said, via ESPN’s Nate Taylor . “I’ll look at everything. item.title: How Max Verstappen beat Red Bull's own simulation tools with P2 in Brazil
item.description: Motorsport photo For the third year in a row, Verstappen produced an impressive comeback drive in the Formula 1 Sao Paulo Grand Prix. While the Dutchman won from 17th on the grid in 2024 and climbed from the pitlane to third place last year, this time he charged from 21st to second. According to Verstappen, his start on the uphill grid did not go to plan, although he took the blame himself after holding the clutch incorrectly, resulting in a slower reaction time. After that, however, the Dutchman made rapid progress. During his first stint on intermediates, he already had the podium positions in his sights, much sooner than Red Bull had ever expected based on its own simulations. "As always, I think no sim in the world will predict that you will go from P21 to P2 or that you get 14 places in 5 laps," Laurent Mekies said post-race in Red Bull’s hospitality unit. "There is no sim able to do that. So, Max is beating the simulations on a regular basis." When the first frontrunners came into the pits at the end of lap 16 to swap their intermediates for slicks, Verstappen was running fifth, although the balance of his RB22 no longer felt the same afterwards. According to the four-time world champion, this was not simply down to the effect slick tyres might have had on the car balance, as the RB22 also felt very different from the opening stages during the closing laps, which were once again completed on intermediates. Red Bull had already acknowledged during the race that it could see a loss of rear downforce in the data, although Mekies says further investigation is needed to establish exactly what caused it. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team Earlier this year, Verstappen complained more than once about 'car degradation', which is why the four-time world champion also took a look at the rear of his car immediately after climbing out to see whether there was any visible damage. "You may have heard Max being fairly vocal with the car balance once we had switched to dry tyres," Mekies admitted. "From that point onwards, he has been very, very unhappy with the car balance, including when we came back to the inters at the very end. So we’ll need to analyse what happened there, how much of that is explaining our time loss and whether or not that would have been enough to fight with McLaren ." item.description: Barcelona superstar to miss Spain’s Czech Republic match after suffering knee discomfort against Atletico Madrid Barcelona have been handed a fitness concern after Lamine Yamal reported discomfort in his right knee following their 2-1 victory over Atletico Madrid . As a result, according to Mundo Deportivo , the forward will remain in Barcelona rather than travel with Spain for Thursday’s Nations League fixture against the Czech Republic, with his availability for the meeting with England on November 15 still dependent on his recovery. The outlet mentions that Yamal underwent medical tests after Sunday’s match at the Metropolitano, and the decision was taken for him to continue his recovery in Barcelona. Indeed, the Spanish international is expected to join Luis de la Fuente’s squad in the coming days, but his participation against England cannot yet be considered certain. Yamal to miss Spain’s trip to face Czech Republic Spain are scheduled to face the Czech Republic in Prague on November 12 before hosting England at the Metropolitano three days later. Lamine Yamal suffered knee discomfort vs Atletico Madrid. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Yamal is expected to miss the first fixture as Barcelona and the national team’s medical staff monitor his condition. The forward was the only Barcelona international to return to the club immediately after the victory over Atletico, while his teammates remained in Madrid ahead of their international commitments. For now, the Royal Spanish Football Federation’s medical department is maintaining contact with Barcelona’s doctors to follow the progress of the affected players. Understandably, the priority will be to assess the 19-year-old’s recovery before deciding whether he can join the national team group and feature in the second fixture. Flick faces another concern over Yamal’s workload The situation is an unwelcome development for Hansi Flick, particularly after Yamal played an important role in Barcelona’s victory against Atletico. It’s important that they do the same with their national teams,” he noted. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images If I told you the Washington Commanders lost a game in which they held the NFL’s eighth-best third-down offense to a 21 percent conversion rate, limited the sixth-best red-zone offense to a 50 percent success rate, and forced two turnovers against the league’s fourth-best offense while surrendering just 20 points, would you believe me? Yes? Well, I’d believe me, too. When the same mistakes and shortcomings keep plaguing a team week after week, you eventually have to accept that the team is exactly what it has shown you. For the Commanders, that reality has become increasingly difficult to ignore after their 20-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, dropping Washington to 2-5-1. Dan Quinn at the podium: "We have not nailed our complimentary football, and I'll keep saying it until we do. " — Martenzie Johnson (@10zJohnson) November 8, 2026 Time is running out on Dan Quinn and the Commanders, and the urgency surrounding their season is growing with every passing week. Few expected Washington to knock off Los Angeles heading into Sunday’s matchup, but the Commanders had a legitimate opportunity to pull off the upset. More importantly, Quinn’s defense gave the offense every opportunity to make it happen. Instead, Washington wasted one of its better defensive performances of the season. After jumping out to a 10-3 lead, the Commanders’ offense completely unraveled. Over their next eight possessions, excluding the final drive, Washington averaged just 4.5 plays and 15 yards per possession while turning the ball over. An offense that had an opportunity to seize control of the game suddenly couldn’t sustain a drive long enough to give its defense a breather, much less put additional points on the board. Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford struggled with his accuracy throughout the afternoon, and multiple drops from his receivers only compounded those issues. Washington’s pass rush wasn’t particularly effective, either, ranking 27th in Week 9 pressure percentage, according to SumerSports. Yet despite its inability to consistently disrupt Stafford, the defense did enough to keep the Rams within striking distance. That’s what makes this loss particularly frustrating. The Commanders didn’t need an extraordinary offensive performance to win. They needed competence, consistency, and the ability to capitalize on the opportunities their defense created. They couldn’t deliver any of the three. The problems start with roster construction, and Sunday’s loss exposed just how significant those shortcomings have become.
